headline: Red Sox keep rolling in Tampa as the stretch run tightens
morning_brew: I was pacing around the living room during that final frame like a caged tiger, but the Sox managed to hold off the Rays for a win that feels like a massive exhale. Roman Anthony was absolutely locked in at the plate, carrying the offense and driving in runs when it mattered most. We were in control for most of the night, and watching the team play with this kind of poise on the road is exactly what I wanted to see with the playoffs looming on the horizon.

Ranger Suarez gave us a massive performance on the mound, keeping the Rays hitters off balance for almost six full innings. It is such a relief to see a starter go out there and handle his business without needing the bullpen to bail him out of a jam every single time. Even when the arson squad had to take over, they kept their cool and prevented any kind of late-game collapse, which is a massive upgrade from the heart-attack finishes we endured earlier this month. I haven't seen an outing this stress-free since neighbor Rick finally stopped trying to build that makeshift batting cage in his driveway.

We are right back at it at Tropicana Field this afternoon, and I am hoping for more of the same consistency to keep the momentum building. There is no time to get comfortable with the schedule we have ahead of us, but seeing this group fight for every out makes me feel a lot better about our chances. I will be glued to the TV again when they take the field, just praying we can keep this rhythm going as we push toward the final weekend of the regular season.
